name: loopcom
title: LOOPCOM
description: Yiddish-to-English call and voicemail translation. Telecom SaaS, vertical social-first advertising.
styleSuffix: Visual language: a sophisticated telecommunications interface in deep navy-black. Premium glass surfaces, precise cyan edge lighting, restrained glow, thin circuit paths, generous negative space, subtle particles, realistic reflections, polished commercial motion design. Use only these colors: luminous mint #5EEAD4, rich teal #14B8A6, bright technology blue #0EA5E9, white, and deep navy-black #020A12. One continuous controlled composition with a very slow small-amplitude push-in and no abrupt cuts. No people and no live-action footage. Render no on-screen text of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, captions, subtitles, labels, logos or watermarks anywhere in the frame. Keep the centre and lower third visually calm and uncluttered so typography can be composited afterwards.
negativePrompt: text, words, letters, numbers, typography, captions, subtitles, labels, logos, watermarks, signage, people, human figures, faces, hands, live-action footage, camera shake, abrupt cuts, extreme zoom, rotation, aspect-ratio change, purple, pink, orange, red, yellow, clutter, flicker, duplicated icons, morphing shapes
rules: Typography is composited in post, never rendered by Veo. Leave clean space for it.
Draft on the lite tier, approve the composition, then render once on the final tier.
Hold a seed across iterations so a prompt edit reads as a real change.
No people. The brand language excludes them, and the Yiddish-speaking market this serves commonly avoids depicting people in advertising.
Keep prompts under roughly 200 words. Long prompts dilute attention and drop elements.
